claims.text: Introducing nanoscale oxide dispersions into a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its mechanical performance under high-temperature conditions.
Introducing nanoscale oxide dispersions into a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its mechanical performance under irradiation.
An oxide-dispersion-strengthened refractory high-entropy alloy will maintain thermal stability.
An oxide-dispersion-strengthened refractory high-entropy alloy will maintain irradiation stability.
Nanoscale Y2O3 or TiO2 dispersions can be incorporated into the alloy matrix by powder metallurgy or mechanical alloying followed by sintering.
The intervention will form stable oxide particles uniformly distributed within the alloy matrix.
The dispersed oxide particles will act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Dislocation pinning by the oxide particles will reduce dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility will enhance creep resistance.
The oxide particles will trap irradiation-induced defects.
Trapping irradiation-induced defects will prevent their aggregation and improve irradiation stability.
Above 1000 °C, the oxide-containing alloy will have higher yield strength than the oxide-free baseline under otherwise identical conditions.
Above 1000 °C, the oxide-containing alloy will have a lower creep rate than the oxide-free baseline under otherwise identical conditions.
Under neutron or ion irradiation, the oxide-containing alloy will retain greater microstructural stability than the oxide-free baseline.
Agglomeration of the oxide dispersions may prevent the predicted improvements.
Interactions between the oxides and alloy matrix may cause undesirable phase transformations that prevent the predicted improvements.
